original_recipe.mass_definition: Terminal product inventory P[g/L]*V[L]/1000. No harvest occurs before96h; stopped batches count zero produced/released product.

evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.29 mg/L at t=50.0 h to 2.05 at t=50.2, then 1.56, 1.92, 1.81, 1.73, 1.62, 1.72, 1.59, 1.47, 1.25 mg/L through t=52.0 h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint.
No DO2 recovery trend over the last ~2 h; the deficit persists at decision time.
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show healthy DO2 (~9-13 mg/L) throughout the same period, indicating this is a receiving-specific process excursion, not a shared input artifact.

Delayed assay: receiving P = 3.11 g/L at t=48 h (available t=52), still on an increasing trajectory versus 1.13 g/L at t=36 h — production is active and worth preserving, ruling out stop (zero counted production) and favoring only mild feed moderation.

Allowed action bounds: increase_air [1.0, 1.15] alone may be insufficient for a >9 mg/L DO deficit; strong_feed_reduction [0.6 feed, 1.15 air] risks excessive product-mass loss; combined [0.8 feed, 1.15 air] attacks oxygen deficit from both sides.
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation suffers a severe, persistent dissolved-oxygen excursion: DO2 fell from ~11.3 mg/L at t=50.0 h to ~1.25-2.0 mg/L between t=50.2 and t=52.0 h, breaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint with no recovery over ~2 h. This demands intervention. I compared the bounded options: (1) increase_air (1.0 feed, 1.15 air) improves oxygen transfer but the 15% ceiling may be insufficient to close a >9 mg/L deficit if demand keeps climbing; (2) reduce_feed (0.8 feed, 1.0 air) lowers oxygen demand but leaves aeration unchanged, risking a slow recovery; (3) strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed) would restore DO fastest but sacrifices product mass, which the task requires retaining; (4) stop yields zero counted production and is unjustified; (5) keep fails the oxygen constraint. The combined action (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) acts on both oxygen supply and demand simultaneously: the modest 20% feed cut reduces oxygen uptake rate while the maximum permitted 15% air increase raises transfer capacity, restoring DO2 above the 2.0 mg/L floor promptly while keeping the culture producing. Source batches (source-1/2/3) show no such DO2 collapse at comparable times (~10-11 mg/L at t=50-52), indicating a receiving-specific event (e.g., higher OUR at scale), not a routine behavior needing no action.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters (actual OUR, kLa, substrate state) are unknown, so the magnitude of recovery under 0.8/1.15 bounds is uncertain; if the demand excursion is very large, DO may remain marginal even under combined action, in which case strong_feed_reduction would be the fallback. Conversely, if the DO dip reflects a transient sensor or brief metabolic surge, increase_air alone could suffice and the feed cut would slightly slow production. P measurements lag 4 h, so the current true product concentration and the effect of the feed cut on production rate cannot be confirmed at decision time.

evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.29 mg/L at 50.0 h to 2.05 at 50.2 h and remains 1.2-2.0 mg/L through 52 h (receiving_observations), violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO2 prior to 50 h tracked sources (~11-13 mg/L); P assay at 48 h = 3.11 g/L matches sources (3.0-3.1 g/L), so growth is normal and the fault is oxygen supply
physical_forward_model at h 52 estimates transfer multiplier ~0.407 of nominal, indicating aeration/transfer failure

Forward-model comparison: strong_feed_reduction yields lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (7.27 mg·h/L) and highest min DO (0.92 mg/L) while retaining ~194 kg product; increase_air alone (deficit 11.61) is insufficient at 40% transfer capacity
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~50.2 h to 1.2-2.0 mg/L (below the 2.0 mg/L minimum) while product formation tracked the source batches, indicating a sudden loss of oxygen-transfer capacity (model-estimated multiplier ~0.41 of nominal). A 15% aeration increase alone cannot close the deficit; the forward model consistently shows strong_feed_reduction (40% feed cut, 15% more air) gives the smallest residual oxygen deficit and highest minimum DO while retaining full product mass (~194 kg). Stop is rejected as it yields zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; even under strong feed reduction, sensitivity members show residual DO violations (min DO range ~0.5-1.4 mg/L), so full constraint satisfaction is not guaranteed. If the transfer failure partially self-recovers or is worse than estimated, the ranking of feed cuts vs aeration could shift, but strong feed reduction is the least-violating option across members and costs no product mass.
